$comment: The two wordlists the hypothesis matcher runs on. This file is the ONE place they
live; the Python engine reads it at import and the JS block is GENERATED by
tools/sync_tiers.py. Edit THIS file, never either runtime's source.
Why: both lists were hand-duplicated in both builds. A review noted there was no
LIST-level guard - parity asserts the functions exist and conformance exercises two of
twenty-two negators - so adding a word to one build only would pass every check and
drift silently for every word no case happens to cover. The tier rules and the depth
budgets were moved here for the same reason after drifting exactly that way.
`stopwords` are dropped before overlap is scored. Note `not` is one of them, which is
precisely why a flat negation scored 1.000 and needed a separate categorical check.
`negators` are the words that check looks for.
